ko: 회사에 큰 변화가 있었어.
en: Actually, there's been a big change at my company.

ko: 워크숍 가 있을 때 알게 됐어. 나한테 묻지도 않고 결정해서 좀 당황했어.
en: I found out while I was at a workshop. They decided without even asking me, so it kinda caught me off guard.
note: 통보받다 = found out · 당황 = caught off guard (embarrassed ✗)

ko: 처음엔 좀 헷갈리고 답답했는데, 돌아와 보니 막상 나쁘지 않아.
en: It was kinda confusing and frustrating at first, but now that I'm back, it's actually not that bad.

ko: 예전 팀에서는 좀 구식 기술로 일했어.
en: On my old team, I was working with kinda outdated tech.

ko: 새 팀에서는 최신 기술을 배우고 써볼 수 있어서 좋았어.
en: On the new team, I got to learn and use the latest stuff, which I really liked.

ko: 근데 다시 원래 팀으로 옮겨져서 썩 좋진 않아.
en: But now I got moved back, so I'm not too happy about it.

ko: 열심히 했는데 못 한 거면 괜찮았을 텐데, 솔직히 열심히 안 한 것 같아.
en: If he'd actually tried and still couldn't do it, I'd be okay with it. But honestly, I don't think he really tried.
note: he'd tried = he had tried · I'd be = I would be

ko: 이번 주말엔 별일 없어. 회사 동료 결혼식만 가면 돼.
en: Not much going on this weekend. I've just got a coworker's wedding to go to.
note: the wedding ceremony of my coworker ✗

ko: 회사에서 친하게 지내는 동료 중 한 명이야.
en: She's one of the coworkers I'm close with.

ko: 결혼식 전에 얼굴 보고 얘기하려고 오늘 만났어.
en: I met up with her today to catch up before the wedding.
note: meet up with = 약속 잡고 만나다 · catch up = 밀린 얘기

ko: 한국에선 보통 현금을 줘. 다들 80달러 정도 내.
en: In Korea, you usually give cash. People usually give around 80 bucks.

ko: 친구가 미국 남자랑 결혼해서 지금 미국에 살아.
en: A friend of mine lives in the US now — she married an American guy.

ko: 장소를 빌려서 그냥 파티를 열더라고.
en: They just rented a venue and threw a party.
note: take a party ✗ → throw a party

ko: 10월치고 좀 쌀쌀한 것 같아.
en: It's kinda chilly for October, huh?

ko: 보통 회사에서 먹어서 장은 거의 안 봐.
en: I usually eat at work, so I barely ever go grocery shopping.

ko: 끝났을 때 무슨 내용인지 잘 모르겠더라. 좀 애매했거든.
en: When it ended, I didn't really get what it was about — it was pretty ambiguous.

ko: 그래서 리뷰랑 인터뷰를 찾아봤더니 그제야 이해가 됐어.
en: So I looked up some reviews and interviews, and then it finally clicked.

ko: 영어 공부하기 좋은 유튜브 채널 알아?
en: Do you know any good YouTube channels for learning English?

ko: 동료 결혼식 갔는데 신랑이 노래할 줄은 몰랐어!
en: I went to my coworker's wedding, and I totally didn't expect the groom to sing!
note: the wedding ceremony of my coworker ✗ · expect + 사람 + to V

ko: 평소에 얘기 잘 안 하던 사람들이랑도 어울릴 수 있었어.
en: I got to hang out with a bunch of people I don't usually talk to.
note: ~할 수 있었다 = got to · not familiar with me ✗

ko: 요즘 결혼식은 대부분 1부 2부로 나뉘어.
en: These days, a lot of weddings have two parts.

ko: 예식 끝나면 약간 뒤풀이 같은 게 있어.
en: After the ceremony, there's kind of an after-party.
note: 명사 앞엔 a little bit ✗ → kind of

ko: 신부가 나를 부모님께 제일 친한 동료라고 소개해줬어.
en: The bride introduced me to her parents as one of her closest coworkers.
note: introduce A to B as C

ko: 고수는 별로야.
en: I'm not a big fan of cilantro.

ko: 아직 그 맛이 익숙하지 않아.
en: I'm just not used to the taste yet.

ko: 친구가 소개해줬어.
en: A friend set us up.

ko: 소개팅 같은 거였어.
en: It was kind of a blind date.

ko: 요즘 한국은 취업 시장이 꽤 힘들어.
en: The job market in Korea is pretty rough these days.

ko: 한국 사람들은 엄청 경쟁적이야.
en: People in Korea are super competitive.

ko: 나라는 작은데 다들 서울에 살아.
en: It's a tiny country, and most people live in Seoul.

ko: 새 프로젝트 잘 되고 있어.
en: The new project's going really well.
note: going in a very good way ✗ → going well (튜터)

ko: 요즘 AI가 너무 빨리 바뀌어서 따라갈 게 많아.
en: AI's moving so fast these days, so there's a lot to keep up with.
note: a lot of work to follow ✗ → keep up with

ko: 올해는 연말인데도 별로 한가하지 않아.
en: Even the end of the year isn't that chill this year.

ko: 개발자 아닌 친구들이 맨날 나 타자 빠르다고 해.
en: My friends who aren't developers always tell me I type really fast.
note: friends who is ✗ · 늘 하는 말은 현재형

ko: 요즘 신입들은 취업하느라 애먹는대.
en: I've heard a lot of new grads are having a hard time finding jobs.
note: are hard to find ✗ → have a hard time -ing

ko: 우린 이제 거의 AI 코드 검토만 해.
en: We're basically just reviewing AI's code now.
note: the reviewer of AI's code ✗ → 동사로

ko: 동료들이랑 미래 얘기하면 좀 무서워져.
en: Whenever my coworkers and I talk about the future, we get kinda scared.
note: I and my coworkers ✗ → my coworkers and I

ko: AI가 번 돈을 다 같이 똑같이 나누면 좋겠다.
en: If the money AI makes got split equally between all of us, that'd be great.
note: 가정법: if절에 will ✗ · the money (that) AI makes

ko: 그 표현 자주 써?
en: Do you guys use it a lot?

ko: 요즘 한국 경기가 별로 안 좋아.
en: The economy's not great in Korea right now.

ko: 이 업무는 우선순위가 낮아서 일단 뒤로 미뤘어요.
en: It's low priority, so I put it on the back burner for now.
note: put behind ✗ (= 잊고 털어내다) · priority is low ✗ → it's low priority
